Subject: Rate card request + how streaming charges handle partial generations

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost breakdown were helpful. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple concrete questions so we can complete our internal TCO: 

1) If a streaming response is interrupted (client disconnects) after N tokens, do you bill only the tokens emitted or do you bill tokens the model generated but weren't delivered?
2) If a retry occurs (client reconnects and we resend the request), how are tokens billed for the retried portion?
3) Do partial generations (when the model times out or aborts) get prorated differently from completed responses?

Can you also send the latest hosted API baseline pricing and any notes on committed volume discounts? We want to model 6–9 month consumption scenarios.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Lina
Director of Product
MedSync Health

Subject: Re: Rate card request + how streaming charges handle partial generations

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Karthik (pricing) and Sean (support/observability) to make sure we give concrete, audit-friendly answers.

I'll attach our current public rate card and a short appendix that breaks down streaming edge cases. Short answers below; Karthik will expand with numbers and a CSV of examples.

- Disconnects: billed for tokens the backend marked as generated (i.e., tokens emitted server-side). If the client disconnects before receiving the final bytes, we've historically charged for generated tokens because the work was completed on our side.
- Retries: if the retry triggers a new model inference (not served from cache/KV), that new generation is billed separately. If you replay the same request and the response is identical and served from cache, we do not double-charge for cached tokens.
- Partial generations/timeouts: we bill for the tokens the model emitted prior to the abort. There is no special prorating aside from the actual token count.

Karthik — can you add the baseline hosted API rate card lines and two example invoice scenarios (disconnect at token 45, retry with full 150-token generation) in the appendix? Also flag where committed discounts would apply.

Lina — forwarding our Redwood_RateCard_v3.pdf. If you want a modeled sheet for your 6–9 month scenarios, send estimated monthly token volumes and we will run the math.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Marcus / Lina — thanks for the excellent questions. I pulled some sample invoice scenarios into the streaming-pricing-appendix.csv attached and summarized below (numbers are illustrative, final will be in the sheet).

Summary (baseline hosted API):
- Token unit price (baseline): $0.0009 per generated token (example)
- Streaming: charged at the same per-token rate; billing counts tokens the runtime marked as generated.

Edge-case examples we included in the CSV: 
1) Client disconnect at token 45: invoice records 45 tokens billed. No further charges unless you replay and that replay performs a new generation.
2) Retry that triggers a fresh generation (150 tokens): invoice records 150 tokens for that retry + any earlier billed attempts.
3) Safety-filter truncation on server-side: billed tokens = tokens generated up to the truncation point. If truncation occurs before completion, it's billed the same as any partial generation. We do not retroactively credit safety truncations.

Committed discounts / smallest acceptable 12mo commit:
- Standard small-commit tier: $25k/month committed (12mo) -> ~10% discount off baseline unit price.
- Mid-tier: $100k/month -> ~18% discount + dedicated support SLA improvements.
- Enterprise: custom pricing above $250k/month with volume-based tiers, latency SLO, and potential on-prem options.

Notes: discounts apply to baseline per-token rates and are reflected on monthly invoices once the commit is active (we pro-rate the month the commitment starts). Credits for chargeback scenarios (e.g., demonstrable double charges from a Redwood bug) are handled case-by-case and require support ticket + invoice review.

Attachment: streaming-pricing-appendix.csv (CSV, 12KB)

> We bill generated tokens up to the truncation; safety truncation is not treated as a free or credit event by default.

Thanks Karthik — that helps. Couple more practical clarifications before we model the commit: 

- If we implement client-side retries that re-send the same request idempotently and Redwood deduplicates at the runtime layer, do you treat that as cache-served (no double charge) or as a new generation? We want to design our retry strategy to avoid accidental double billing.
- In logged examples, can you show invoice line items as they would appear for: (a) disconnect+no retry; (b) disconnect+client retry that causes new generation; (c) server safety truncation mid-output. Our finance team prefers to see mock invoice lines.

If everything looks good we can propose a $60k/month 12-mo commitment to start (roughly middle of your small-commit tier). What would the effective unit price be and can you include a sample invoice and a draft contract?

Best,
Lina

Lina / Marcus — appreciate the concrete ask and the proposed commitment. Action items and responses below: 

1) Retry deduplication: if your retry is idempotent and the runtime can safely dedupe (same request id, same prompt, cache hit), we will not bill twice. We added a short note in the CSV with the dedupe behavior and the idempotency header you should set. If the retry causes a fresh inference, that execution is billed.

2) Mock invoice lines: attached is a one-page sample invoice (included in the CSV appendix). Quick snapshot of sample lines (effective unit price assumes $60k/mo commit -> ~12% discount off baseline):
   - Invoice line: 'Hosted API - Generated tokens (streaming): 45 tokens @ $0.000792 = $0.03564'  (case: disconnect, no retry)
   - Invoice line: 'Hosted API - Generated tokens (streaming): 150 tokens @ $0.000792 = $0.1188' (case: retry that triggered new generation)
   - Invoice line: 'Hosted API - Generated tokens (streaming): 95 tokens @ $0.000792 = $0.07524' (case: safety truncation at token 95)

3) Contract / next steps: I've uploaded a draft proposal to DocuSign and attached a PDF for your review (docusign-proposal-med-sync-20261121.pdf). If acceptable, sign and we'll route to finance to finalize the monthly commitment and set up billing.

I'll ask Finance to set up a dedicated billing SKU for the committed pricing so your invoices clearly show discounted unit rates. Sean, please keep an eye on any support tickets about dedupe edge cases while they ramp.

Marissa Cole
